subject: Renewal bridge: co-term + midterm capacity add — pricing options
messages:
From: Ben Holloway <ben@acuityhealth.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: Sara Lim <sara.lim@acuityhealth.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Mid-contract capacity bump & co-term question

Sean —

Quick one: our usage for the pilot exceeded projections in Q1 and we need to bump capacity for the next two quarters. Current contract runs until 12/31/2027 and procurement is asking whether we can: 1) add a mid-contract capacity uplift starting June 1, and 2) align (co-term) the expanded commitment to our existing renewal date so we don’t have staggered invoices.

Two specific asks from my side:
- Can you give a ballpark increase in ARR for a +40% capacity uplift (service tier stays the same)?
- Is there a standard pro-rata approach you use for mid-term increases, and would there be any additional discount for moving the uplift onto our existing renewal (co-term)?

I can loop procurement if you need an official PO path. We’re aiming to avoid a full RFP but do need pricing on paper to move forward.

Thanks —
Ben
Director of Platform Engineering
Acuity Health

Attachments: Acuity_MCP_usage_report_Q1.csv (csv)
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Ben Holloway <ben@acuityhealth.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 17:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Mid-contract capacity bump & co-term question

Ben —

Thanks for the heads up and the usage file — I skimmed it and this is a good problem to have. High-level answers up front so you can share with procurement:

1) Ballpark uplift: for a +40% capacity add, estimated incremental ARR (annualized) is roughly $126k based on your current effective unit price and token mix. I’ll attach a worked example.

2) Pro-rata approach: we typically pro-rate the delta for the remainder of the current term, then offer a one-time transition credit if you agree to co-term the uplift to the existing renewal date. That credit ranges from 5–12% depending on total committed spend and whether you sign a 12 vs 24 month co-term extension.

Options we can put on paper:
- Option A: Mid-term add only (no co-term). Pro-rate June–Dec at list, no additional credit. Quickest to approve.
- Option B: Mid-term add + co-term to 12/31/2027. Pro-rate June–Dec, plus 6% one-time co-term credit applied to the uplift ARR if you sign a 12-month extension on top of current term.
- Option C: Mid-term add + 24-month co-term (extend renewal to 12/31/2029). Pro-rate June–Dec, plus 10% one-time credit and commit to a 24-month reserved capacity discount schedule.

For procurement: we can provide a redlineable amendment and a DocuSign link. If you want this to be revenue-neutral for Acuity in the current fiscal quarter, Option A is fastest. If procurement wants predictable unit economics and to avoid re-negotiation in 6 months, Option B is the usual tradeoff.

I’ll loop in Nikhil from sales ops for exact numbers and Monica from CS for impact to SLOs and on-call.

Next steps: tell me which option procurement prefers and I’ll draft amendment language + a PO-ready summary.

Best,
Sean Gallagher
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
sean.gallagher@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0116
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Apr 2027 09:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Internal: Acuity mid-contract add — pricing/legal ops

Team —

Acuity asked for +40% capacity starting 2027-06-01 and wants the uplift co-termed to 12/31/2027. I proposed three options to them (A/B/C) — see my note to Ben below. Need quick alignment on:

- Nikhil: can you validate the incremental ARR calc and produce a clean two-column quote (current vs post-uplift) and the 6%/10% credit math for co-term options?
- Monica: will the +40% have any impact on SLOs or routing? If yes, propose mitigations (burst capacity windows, autoscale safety limits).
- Lauren: any legal concerns with a one-time credit applied as a line-item on an amendment (rather than retro credits)? We want clean accounting for procurement.
- Dev: ops — how quickly can we stand up an additional capacity pool and is June 1 feasible?

Acuity is a mid-market account but strategic in health vertical; procurement wants a simple PO path. If we proceed with Option B, procurement has requested a PDF proposal and a DocuSign-ready amendment.

Can I get numbers by EOD tomorrow? I’ll try to keep Ben in the loop but hold off external comms until we have the quote attached.

Thanks —
Sean
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Ben Holloway <ben@acuityhealth.com>
Cc: Sara Lim <sara.lim@acuityhealth.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 22 Apr 2027 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Mid-contract capacity bump & co-term question

Ben —

Appreciate the quick turnaround on the usage file. Attached is a short proposal (redwood_co-term_proposal_0422.pdf) that summarizes the three options and has the exact ARR math. Highlights:

- Option A (no co-term): pro-rated June–Dec, incremental ARR $126,400 (no credit).
- Option B (co-term to 12/31/2027 + 12-month extension): pro-rated June–Dec, incremental ARR $126,400 with a one-time 6% co-term credit = $7,584 credit applied to the uplift line item. We can sign an amendment to document this and close via PO + DocuSign.
- Option C (24-month co-term): 10% one-time credit and staged reserved capacity pricing (detailed in attachment).

If procurement wants a single invoice cadence, Option B is the usual path — we’ll absorb the credit up-front and reflect it on the amendment so it’s visible to their finance team. I’ve also included a sample amendment snippet in the PDF.

If this looks acceptable, I’ll: 1) open a DocuSign envelope, 2) prepare an amendment with line-item credit, and 3) coordinate with Dev/Infra for June activation. Linking the DocuSign here: https://www.docusign.com/placeholder/abc123

Next step from your side: confirm Option (A/B/C) and whether procurement will route via PO or needs an inter-company invoice.

Best,
Sean Gallagher
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_co-term_proposal_0422.pdf (pdf)
